players.product: bring-your-own-power combined-cycle gas generation for hyperscale data centers (1.2 GW Texas project; 5.4 GW of GE Vernova turbine / Kiewit EPC slots)

quarterly_data.signal: FY2025 results (CEO/CFO): a record year, with full year adjusted EPS of $8.24 per share and adjusted EBITDA of $4.087 billion, both above the high end of raised guidance and up 21% and 8% year over year; adjusted net income $1.606 billion; free cash flow before growth $2.210 billion or $11.63 per share, up $148 million or 7%. Segment adjusted EBITDA: Texas $1.877 billion, East $981 million, West and Other $137 million, Smart Home $1.092 billion. It was the third consecutive year NRG raised its outlook and delivered above it.
quarterly_data.figure: adjusted EPS $8.24; adjusted EBITDA $4.087 billion; FCFbG $2.210 billion ($11.63 per share)

quarterly_data.signal: Data center contracting in 2025 (CEO): 'We signed 445 megawatts of long-term data center PPAs at attractive margins.' The long-term plan includes the portion of those 445 megawatts expected online during the period. The CEO said these deals are 'smaller than the other ones we've been discussing' (distinct from the large gig-plus hyperscaler deals) and that this retail channel is still 'a great channel that we'll continue to pursue'.
quarterly_data.figure: 445 megawatts of long-term data center PPAs signed in 2025

quarterly_data.signal: Large-load growth opportunity (CEO): 'We have the ability today to support more than 6 gigs of long-term power agreements to serve large data center demand. At that level, it represents the potential to add more than $2.5 billion of recurring annual adjusted EBITDA on contracts of up to 20 years.' The more than 6 gigs of natural gas generation capacity reserved for customer-backed large load projects includes 5.4 gigs through NRG's GEV and Kiewit venture and 1 gig of upgrade potential in the acquired LS Power portfolio; the CEO confirmed the $2.5 billion corresponds to 'roughly 6 gigs'. For 2026 NRG targets 'at least or a minimum of 1 gigawatt' of signed long-term data center power contracts under its Bring Your Own Power approach, and that amount is not included in 2026 guidance or the roll-forward outlook. 'Discussions are ongoing, so stay tuned.'
quarterly_data.figure: more than 6 gigs; more than $2.5 billion of recurring annual adjusted EBITDA; 5.4 gigs + 1 gig of upgrade potential; 2026 target at least 1 gigawatt

quarterly_data.signal: Large-load deal structure (CEO/President): NRG is 'looking at blocks in excess of 1 gig', 'contracts of minimum 10 and frequently 20 years with investment-rated entities', with 'a significant fixed price component'. The first ('the first tower, assuming we get to the place we need to get') 'could be on by the end of late '29 and then ratably probably 1 gig a year, maybe more for each year after that.' The structure the hyperscalers 'seem to be okay with' is 'a very heavy capacity payment' plus a variable component that 'turns into basically a heat rate for the hyperscaler. They take the gas risk.' NRG can help them offload that gas risk through its gas platform. On counterparty credit, NRG is selective 'even inside of the universe of hyperscalers.'
quarterly_data.figure: blocks in excess of 1 gig; contracts of minimum 10 and frequently 20 years; first by late '29; then 1 gig a year

quarterly_data.signal: Data center pricing and returns (President/CFO): the price target was adjusted 'to an $80-plus kind of range', but building '1.2 gigawatts of GEV turbines' puts the price at the high end: 'think north of the $90 to $95 range where we were back in our original guidance.' 'It's got to pay for the equipment. It's got to pay for our return, and we're not going to do a deal unless it does.' $95 is 'a representation of the bottom end of what the total value looks like from a capacity and variable component'. Because the deals are very heavy on capacity, that value does not map cleanly to a $/MWh price. Deals on NRG sites also involve a land transaction that is not in that number. NRG gets its return and capital back inside the 20-year contract and is 'one of the few people who've got 9 turbines that people can go put on the ground'. Every project must clear the 12% to 15% pretax unlevered hurdle rate. The CFO expects corporate-style balance sheet financing at roughly the corporate 3x leverage level, not project financing, while keeping at least a $1 billion buyback program.
quarterly_data.figure: $80-plus kind of range; north of the $90 to $95 range; $95 bottom end; 12% to 15% pretax unlevered hurdle; 9 turbines

quarterly_data.signal: Bridge power (President): 'Bridge Power that works is a limited resource out there today'. The technology NRG views as most successful is 'overengineered reciprocating engines'. Bridge power lets a hyperscaler scale up capacity while the CCGT is being built. NRG has 'agreements with Bridge Power providers' (not named) and can offer that limited resource as part of a package to hyperscalers. Some hyperscaler clients want it; others will simply absorb the CCGTs when they come on.

LS Power acquisition closed at the end of January (CEO/CFO): NRG's generation fleet 'has doubled to 25 gigawatts', adding 18 natural gas assets, mainly in PJM with more in ERCOT, NYISO and ISO New England. The combined fleet is now more than 75% natural gas, and performance is already beating underwriting assumptions on stronger capacity and energy prices. CPower adds a commercial and industrial demand response platform. Several acquired PJM peaking units offer a potential 1 gigawatt of upgrades through conversion to combined cycle. In PJM the initial focus will be 'the 1 gig of uprates' ('faster and quicker to market'), with 'probably the other 5.4 outside of PJM'. Engineers are assessing the 1,000 megawatts of uprates plus possible '25 or 50-megawatt clips' given the RBA, with NRG 'looking for opportunities to monetize that through hyperscalers'. The 2026 plan includes $950 million of free cash flow before growth from the LS Power assets (prorated to 11 months) and $123 million of one-time integration costs.
quarterly_data.figure: 25 gigawatts; 18 natural gas assets; more than 75% natural gas; 1 gig of uprates in PJM; $950 million FCFbG (11 months)

quarterly_data.signal: Market pace (CEO/President): in PJM, data-center contracting 'was going to be slower than Texas. It's still going to be slower than Texas', though progress is being made: 'It's just faster outside of PJM at this moment.' ERCOT's batching approach to large-load interconnection is 'a great step forward to accelerate the process for people to get data centers and large loads interconnected to the grid', compared with a serial process. CEO framework: 'New large loads must bring their own power and contract for the generation that supports them.'

Long-term outlook rolled forward to 2030 (CEO/CFO): 2026 guidance was reaffirmed (it includes 11 months of LS Power). NRG still targets at least 14% annual growth in adjusted EPS and FCFbG per share, now measured from 2026 through 2030: adjusted EPS of greater than $14 per share and FCFbG of greater than $22 per share by 2030, driven by about an 80-20 split of organic growth versus share repurchases. The plan shows $18.3 billion of total capital available through 2030, including a $13.2 billion return of capital ($11 billion of share repurchases and $2.2 billion of common dividends), plus $2.9 billion of debt reduction to reach 3x net debt to EBITDA. The outlook now includes all 3 Texas Energy Fund projects (the first on track for June 2026 completion, the other 2 by mid-2028) and the portion of the 445 megawatts of data center contracts online in the period. It holds power and capacity prices flat (PJM at the $325 per megawatt day cap for the next 2 auctions), 'does not assume any additional data center contracts or higher power or capacity prices', and excludes the 1 gigawatt of CT to CCGT conversion opportunities.
quarterly_data.figure: adjusted EPS greater than $14 per share by 2030; FCFbG greater than $22 per share; $18.3 billion capital through 2030; $13.2 billion return of capital

quarterly_data.signal: Flexible demand (management): the Texas residential VPP launched in 2025 ended the year at 'nearly 10x our original objective'. NRG is building a 1 gig virtual power plant in Texas and plans to launch a VPP-like program in the East early in the second quarter. With its GoodLeap and Sunrun relationships it keeps scaling batteries and is 'pacing well against the 300-megawatt number' given for 2027. Separately, a series of tolling contracts adds up to over 1 gig of batteries in Texas for the retail portfolio. During Winter Storm Fern the Texas fleet achieved 97% in the money availability.
quarterly_data.figure: VPP at nearly 10x original objective; 300-megawatt 2027 target; over 1 gig batteries in Texas; 97% availability
